_comment: Snapshot of expected hub test counts, from per-file-isolated `bun run check-baseline` (each hub/test file in its own process — Bun's mock.module is process-global and first-write-wins, so a shared process makes the suite order-dependent). The enforced gate is pass_min/skip_max/fail_max; pass/skip/total below are the informational actuals.
captured_from: Bare checkout, NO ambient env, NO database (post-#345, which made this configuration green): `bun run check-baseline` → pass=1827 skip=236 fail=0 total=2063. This is the FLOOR configuration. CI (.woodpecker/qc.yaml) additionally exports REMO_E2E_DB_URL against a real postgres:16 service, which UN-SKIPS the e2e suites — so CI sees strictly MORE passes and FEWER skips than the numbers here. There are no inverse (run-only-without-a-DB) gates, so this floor is valid for both configurations.

tolerance._comment: pass_min is a REAL floor (1800 vs 1827 actual — ~1.5% headroom), not a formality. It was 700 against 1827 actual passes, which meant roughly 1,100 tests could silently stop running and check-baseline would still print OK: a ratchet, not a gate. fail_max:0 only catches tests that RUN and fail — it cannot catch tests that vanish. That is what pass_min is for, so keep it tight. If you legitimately remove tests, lower it deliberately in the same PR and say why. skip_max 245 vs 236 actual: EVERY skip in the suite is REMO_E2E_DB_URL-gated with an explicit reason — there are no unconditional or laundered skips. Keep it that way; a skip added for any other reason is a failure in disguise and must not be absorbed by this budget. fail_max stays 0.
